title: Two-source extraction at log n plus constant entropy
formal: Do a constant C and a deterministic algorithm running in \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) time exist that compute \(E_{n}:\{0,1\}^{n}\times \{0,1\}^{n}\to \{0,1\}\) with |\(\Pr [E_{n}(X,Y)=1]- 1/2|\le 0.01\) for every pair of independent sources X,Y of min-entropy at least \(\log _{2}n+C\)?
definitions: The algorithm receives n and the two n-bit strings, and defines one function for every \(n\ge 1\). A source is any probability distribution on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\); its min-entropy is −\(\log _{2}(\max _{x} \Pr [X=x])\). Independence means the joint law is the product of the two marginal distributions. For n where the entropy threshold exceeds n there are no eligible sources. No auxiliary uniform seed, advice or distribution description is supplied. The constants and time polynomial are universal.

context_blocks.text: Two independent weak sources can contain much randomness while neither source by itself yields even one predictably unbiased bit. The target reaches the entropy threshold permitted by a random truth table with a polynomial-time evaluable function.

Xin Li’s construction achieves entropy \(O(\log  n)\), with an unspecified multiplicative constant. The requested \(\log _{2}n+C\) threshold is stronger than that asymptotic-order statement. This distinction also matters when converting extraction into explicit Ramsey graphs.

why: Reach the information-theoretic entropy threshold for a foundational seedless randomness primitive.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
